methodological_rigor.justification: Solid registry-based cohort design from routine clinical practice with 116,217 eligible samples and passive follow-up through laboratory information system. Statistical approach includes risk ratios, 95% confidence intervals, chi-square tests, and effect sizes. Verification bias acknowledged as a limitation where test-positive women receive more intense follow-up than double-negative women, though this reflects real-world screening practice. Missing elements include pre-specified analysis plan and formal causal inference framework.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (2b) with direct clinical application to cervical cancer screening. Demonstrates strong clinical utility by identifying NILM/mRNA+ subgroup with 13% CIN3+ risk (vs. 0.22% in NILM/mRNA-), providing actionable risk stratification for triage decisions. Results directly interpretable for clinical management without intermediate translation steps. Supports precision screening approach within existing cytology-based programs.

reporting_quality.justification: Study adheres to STROBE checklist with clear reporting of objectives, study design, data sources, outcome definitions, and statistical analysis. Methods section is comprehensive with detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria and 94% inclusion rate documented. Results presented with risk estimates, 95% CIs, and appropriate summary statistics. Data source is regional pathology information system; no explicit public data repository or supplementary materials shared. Authors note de-identification but no data-sharing statement provided.

novelty_literature.justification: Study extends prior evidence on genotype-specific HPV mRNA testing in Norwegian populations to a large real-world routine-practice cohort. Co-testing concept is not novel; HPV mRNA triage is established in literature. Contribution is meaningful but incremental: demonstrates that 3-type mRNA assay produces clinically interpretable risk stratification in everyday practice with long-term follow-up. Does not introduce new methodology or unexpected findings.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear abstract, logical progression of methods/results/discussion. Figures and tables effectively communicate risk gradients and genotype-specific patterns (Tables 1-6). Background section appropriately contextualizes HPV screening evolution. Discussion extensively compares findings to prior studies, with some repetition. Minor clarity gaps in explanation of sample-level versus individual-level unit of analysis and its implications for risk estimates.

key_strengths: Large real-world cohort (116,217 samples) with comprehensive long-term follow-up through December 2025
Clear demonstration of stepwise risk gradient across four co-test categories from NILM/mRNA- (0.22% CIN3+) to ASC-US+/mRNA+ (28.5% CIN3+)
Identifies clinically actionable subgroup: NILM/mRNA+ representing 1.3% of normal cytology but capturing 42.7% of CIN3+ lesions
Genotype-specific analysis shows biologically plausible risk hierarchy (HPV16 > HPV18 > HPV45) supporting clinical interpretability
Detailed methods with explicit outcome definitions, sample flow, and acknowledgment of key limitations including verification bias
key_concerns: Verification bias from differential follow-up between test-positive and double-negative groups; test-positive women more likely to undergo colposcopy, potentially inflating their risk estimates
Mixed clinical population (screening + follow-up + diagnostic testing) rather than pure primary screening cohort; results may not generalize to routine screening alone
Unit of analysis is co-test sample not individual woman; repeated testing in surveillance inflates event counts and may overestimate risks in re-screened cohorts
3-type HPV mRNA assay (PreTect SEE targeting only HPV16/18/45) is targeted rather than broad; does not capture disease from other HR-HPV types, limiting applicability
Strictly observational and descriptive design precludes causal inference; provides risk stratification evidence only
Outcomes for cervical cancer were sparse (126 total cases) with wide confidence intervals, limiting precision of genotype-specific cancer risk estimates
chief_reviewer.rationale: Study is appropriate for Tier 3 (competent, incremental observational work). Methodological rigor and reporting quality are solid, but observational design and limited novelty preclude Tier 2. Real-world applicability and clear clinical stratification support publication, with minor revisions addressing verification bias quantification and generalizability scope.
